title: Skyline Bridge + Redwood Partner GPU Onramp Intro
summary: Introductory partner discovery: Skyline Bridge exploring Redwood as a GPU onramp for their multi-region SaaS. Discussed deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), network/VPC requirements, pilot sizing (H100 vs A100), KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and next step of pilot proposal + network diagram. AE+SE present from Redwood; customer engineering & infra leads attending.
topics: Current infra and constraints (multi-region, low-latency EU/US)
Deployment options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
GPU sizing: A100 80GB vs H100 80GB and per-token cost estimates
Networking: VPC peering, IP allowlists, egress, private control plane
Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML/SCIM, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Pilot scope: workload examples, perf targets, timeline
next_steps: Tom to send partner onboarding deck and preliminary pilot pricing (link + sheet) by 2025-04-27
Priya to propose pilot GPU config and perf expectations (H100 vs A100 baseline) and sample benchmark run instructions by 2025-04-30
Skyline to share network diagram and expected throughput patterns (p95 latency targets, request qps) by 2025-04-28
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive focused on VPC/private control plane on 2025-05-02 (Tentative)
action_items: Tom Baker - share partner deck + pricing spreadsheet - due 2025-04-27
Priya Mehta - draft pilot config (gpu counts, model variants, batch sizes) + benchmarking steps - due 2025-04-30

transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-04-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Tom Baker (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (Skyline - Head Infra), Ana Ruiz (Skyline - CTO), Marcus Chen (Skyline - Platform Eng)
Recording quality: medium; some mis-words and pauses.

[00:00] Tom: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick round robin — i'm tom baker, account lead on the partner program at Redwood. priya's our se. how are you all?
[00:08] Liam: Good, thanks. Liam here. we're keen to understand options for a quick onramp to GPUs for our inference workloads, multi-region mostly US/EU.
[00:14] Ana: Hi folks. i'm ana, CTO. main ask is predictable latency for interactive features + cost control, and we have strong data residency and SOC2 reqs.
[00:22] Priya: Great, thanks. quick agenda — mutual intros, current infra, deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), pilot sizing, and security requirements. we'll leave time for q's. sound ok?
[00:31] Marcus: Yep. Also want to check routing/fallbacks — if one region is out, how do you failover without big latency hit?

[02:05] Tom: Quick background: Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. partner onramp use-case is common — you want us to be the inference plane while you keep control of network and data as needed.
[02:22] Priya: For performance we tune batching, prefix/K-V cache, and quantization. you mentioned p95 targets — what are you aiming for?
[02:30] Ana: Ideally p95 under 250ms for short chat prompts (<=512 tokens), and autoscaling for peak traffic. cost needs to be within our existing budget envelope — can't be 10x.
[02:44] Tom: Ok. quick clarif — are you running the encoder/decoder model in-house today or just CPU-based endpoints?
[02:50] Marcus: We have a CPU transformer fallback for low-volume but it's not acceptable for prod. We're running a small on-prem GPU cluster but scaling it globally is hard.

[04:10] Priya: So typical options — Hosted API: fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, we manage models and runtime. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation. Private (VPC): customer-managed network with private control plane, often chosen for stricter compliance.
[04:28] Liam: For Skyline, data residency and VPC-required for EU customers. We prefer VPC peering and our own KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[04:39] Tom: Yes, we have integrations for KMS and can support HSM in private deployments. for hosted we offer encryption at rest and customer key options in enterprise plans.

[06:00] Priya: On GPU sizing — H100 80GB is best for large context, but A100 80GB is cost-effective for many workloads. For 512-token interactive prompts, an H100 baseline can reduce latency by ~15-25% for some model families. We'll send baseline numbers.
[06:20] Marcus: Do you expose kv cache or prefix caching controls? Our latency spikes come from repeated context assembly.
[06:27] Priya: Yes — prefix/K-V cache is supported in the runtime. we can cache user session prefixes to avoid reprocessing. note transcription sometimes says 'K V cash' which is wrong though — it's K-V cache.

[08:10] Ana: Security — We need SOC2 Type II reports, SAML SSO/SCIM for provisioning, RBAC, audit logs retained 1 year, and fine-grained token scoping. Is that standard?
[08:21] Tom: Those are standard enterprise asks. We provide SOC2 reports under NDA, SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and configurable audit retention for private setups. We'll attach the security pack link after the call.

[10:12] Marcus: Networking: can you do VPC peering + static egress IPs? We also need to avoid public internet egress for EU traffic.
[10:22] Priya: For Private deployments yes — VPC peering, private control plane, static egress, and we can do transit via direct connect equivalents. For Hosted we have IP allowlists and region-based routing but if you need private peering we'll look at Private.

[12:05] Liam: Pricing — for a pilot we want an estimate. say 5k qps peak? that's probably high, maybe bursty. can you give a per-token cost vs dedicated reserved instance?
[12:18] Tom: Short answer — hosted per-token is simplest but higher unit cost. Dedicated gives much lower per-token cost at commit. we'll model a 90-day pilot with reserved capacity vs burst on hosted. i'll include a pilot pricing sheet.

[14:50] Priya: Pilot scoping suggestion: pick representative routes (chat, embeddings, rerank). Start with 2-4 GPUs (H100 or A100 depending on model), 2 region footprint (US/EU), run 48-72h throughput + latency benchmarks with our benchmark tool. We'll provide the script.
[15:05] Marcus: Can we run the benchmark in our environment to validate latency to your endpoints?
[15:12] Priya: Yes — we can provide a dockerized runner. For private we can run inside your VPC to mimic production.

[17:30] Ana: A couple of technical Qs — how do you handle model rollouts and A/B testing? We need safe rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[17:41] Tom: Redwood Console supports canaries, A/B, automatic fallback policies and per-route model pinning. you can set a fallback to a quantized variant to preserve availability.

[19:55] Marcus: Quantization — is rwd-opt-7b-q4 supported? we have a few internal smaller models and would like quantized paths.
[20:03] Priya: Yes, quantized variants are supported; runtime picks kernels based on quantization and sequence lengths. we'll list supported model families in the doc. sometimes names get borked in transcripts — e.g., "rwd-opt" may come out as "rewed opt" in auto text.

[22:40] Liam: Data residency again — for EU customers can you guarantee data stays in EU region for hosted?
[22:48] Tom: We can route EU traffic to EU-hosted clusters and offer private deployments for hard-residency requirements. For strict regs, customers often prefer Private.

[25:00] Ana: Can you do SLA-backed latency? Our legal wants an SLO for median and p95.
[25:08] Tom: Yes on Dedicated and Private we can include latency SLOs in contract. Hosted API may have SLA for uptime but latency SLAs are typically in Dedicated.

[28:12] Marcus: Integration details — SDKs, api keys, token scoping, function calling?
[28:20] Priya: We have REST + official SDKs, streaming responses, function/tool calling and structured output. We also provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Console for observability.

[31:00] Liam: Are there any known gotchas for on-prem customers? firewall rules, kernel driver versions?
[31:09] Priya: For on-prem there's more ops coordination: driver versions, CUDA/cuDNN compatibility, and kernel patches. We'll provide an on-prem checklist. For VPC there's less ops but still network and IAM work.

[34:30] Ana: How do we handle secrets and KMS — can Redwood call our KMS or do we manage keys fully?
[34:39] Tom: In Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM; with Hosted we offer customer-key options in enterprise. We'll map options in the security pack.

[36:55] Marcus: Benchmarks — can priya share a sample spreadsheet with target metrics (p50/p95, throughput, token cost)?
[37:02] Priya: Yes, i'll attach a benchmark template and a sample run from a previous partner.

[39:10] Ana: Timeline — we want a 6-week pilot ideally, starting early May. Does that sound feasible?
[39:18] Tom: Yes. assuming paperwork, network prep and pilot pricing sign-off we can aim for a kickoff in the first week of May.

[41:20] Priya: We'll also suggest a small canary traffic plan so you don't throw full traffic at the new endpoints.

[43:00] Tom: Quick recap: we'll share partner deck + pricing sheet, security pack (SOC2 + SAML details), pilot config & benchmark scripts, and schedule a VPC deep-dive tech call. skyline to share network diagram and workload profile.
[43:20] Ana: Sounds good. Marcus will coordinate the network diagram, i'll loop legal once we get the security doc.

[45:05] Liam: Any blockers we should call out now?
[45:10] Marcus: Only that we need to validate egress routes for EU data — otherwise looks straightforward.

[46:20] Tom: Great; we'll follow up with all artifacts. thanks everyone for the candor.
[46:30] Ana: Thanks, bye.
[46:32] Tom: Bye.

End of transcript. Shared links mentioned during call: https://redwood.example.com/partners/skyline-bridge-deck (partner deck), https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (security pack), spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/skyline-pricing-sheet (pilot pricing).
